rules.text: Documentation must describe what the project actually does today. A claim is not kept when the code contradicts it — an uncomfortable truth is documented, not hidden.
rules.action: The Phase 1 documentation truth pass is the first task of the phase; no feature work or promotion starts before it.

citations.location: Reply to the Phase 1 plan proposal
citations.excerpt: the least thing i want it to be is miss leading

rules.current: Diverges: README.md states "Passwords are never stored — rclient only uses the password during the RustDesk handshake and never logs or persists it", while web/src/components/ConnectForm.tsx persists rclient_password in localStorage.
rules.check: Compare each README/docs claim about behaviour with the code; the password section must match rule PROJ-002.

rules.text: The RustDesk password is only saved in the browser when the user opts in through a "Remember password" checkbox, which is off by default. Without the opt-in, the password is used for the session and not persisted.
rules.action: Add the opt-in checkbox to the connect form (task T10) and document the behaviour truthfully (task T1).
rules.current: Diverges: ConnectForm always writes the password to localStorage (key rclient_password) on connect.
rules.check: Connect with the box unticked and reload: no password in localStorage; tick it, connect, reload: password restored.

rules.text: rclient.linkzy.dev stays the owner's personal production deployment. The public demo runs on the Contabo VPS under its own subdomain, so visitors never reach the owner's private relay.
rules.action: Keep the production URL out of README quickstart as the demo; point the demo link at the new subdomain once it exists.

citations.excerpt: i will keep this as my personal producion deployment since i use it every day to connect to my computers, but we can create a new demo in the  Contabo VPS that i allowed you to access in the connections. we give it another subdomain

rules.current: Diverges: README and docs point at rclient.linkzy.dev as the live demo; the demo instance at rclient-demo.linkzy.dev is not deployed yet (task T18). The owner's production instance stays at rclient.linkzy.dev.
rules.check: Open https://rclient-demo.linkzy.dev — it serves the demo UI, and its relay defaults are public RustDesk servers, not the owner's relay. https://rclient.linkzy.dev keeps serving production.

rules.text: The repository keeps the name rustdesk-custom-web-client: the official RustDesk web client does not work well with self-hosted relays, and that is why this custom client exists.
rules.action: Do not rename the repository; explain the name and the reason in the README's "Why this exists" section.

citations.excerpt: Keep rustdesk-custom-web-client (there is an official client somewhere in the official rustdesk repo, but it does not work nicely, this is the reason i built this custom one)

rules.text: The README's hero visual is static screenshots until the Phase 2 fake RustDesk host exists; then it becomes a GIF/video recorded automatically with Playwright, so it can be regenerated on demand.
